subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
cluster: How plants get the materials to grow
skillName: Plants Get Materials from Air and Water
intro: A growing plant adds a lot of material to its body, such as stems, leaves, and roots. It might seem like this material comes from the soil, but most of it does not. Plants get the materials they need for growth mostly from air and water. Using energy from sunlight, a plant combines carbon dioxide from the air with water to make its own food, and that food builds the plant's body. Soil does provide small amounts of minerals and holds water, but the bulk of a plant's mass comes from air and water, not soil. A classic piece of evidence: when a small tree grows for years in a pot, it gains many pounds of mass while the soil in the pot barely loses any weight.

items.prompt: A tree grows in a pot for five years and gains 50 pounds, but the soil in the pot loses only a few ounces. What does this suggest about where the tree's new material came from?

steps: If the tree's material came from soil, the soil would lose about as much weight as the tree gained.
The soil barely changed, so the material did not mostly come from the soil.
The tree must have gotten most of its new material from air and water instead.
solution.answer: Most of the tree's new material came from air and water, not from the soil.

items.prompt: Explain how a plant uses air and water to build its body.

steps: A plant takes in carbon dioxide gas from the air and water from the ground.
Using energy from sunlight, the plant combines these to make its own food (sugar).
This food is used to build the plant's stems, leaves, and roots, so air and water become plant material.
solution.answer: The plant combines carbon dioxide from the air and water, using sunlight, to make food that builds its body.

items.prompt: A student argues that plants eat soil to grow. Use evidence to build a better argument.

steps: Plants do take some minerals and water from soil, but the amount of soil used is very small.
Experiments show plants gain far more mass than the soil loses.
So the stronger claim is that plants get most of their growth material from air and water, with only small amounts from soil.
solution.answer: Plants get most of their growth material from air and water; soil provides only small amounts of minerals and water.

items.prompt: Name the two main sources of the materials a plant uses to grow.

steps: Plants build their bodies using matter they take in.
The two main sources are air (carbon dioxide) and water.

items.prompt: Two identical plants are grown, one given plenty of water and air and one kept very dry. Predict which grows more and explain why.

steps: Plants need water as a main material for growth, along with air.
The dry plant lacks one of its main growth materials, so it cannot build as much new tissue.
The well-watered plant has both air and water available, so it grows more.
solution.answer: The well-watered plant grows more, because water is one of the main materials plants use to grow.

items.prompt: Why is sunlight important for a plant to turn air and water into new material?

steps: Combining carbon dioxide and water into food requires energy.
The plant captures that energy from sunlight.
Without sunlight the plant cannot make the food it needs to build its body from air and water.
solution.answer: Sunlight provides the energy the plant needs to combine air and water into food for growth.
